\chapter{The correspondence with the C code}\label{chap:correspondence}

The model is checked against ratpoints v3.1.1 (commit \texttt{1a998538dfa8}). The C files below are those of the library and \texttt{main.c}, whose parts that the command-line program does not mirror are to be excluded. Every line of code of them lies in at most one recorded range: a range is either modelled by the Lean declarations named, or excluded from the model with a reason. Each recorded range is checked against the text it had when it was reviewed.

\item \csource{rp-private.h}{133}{133}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}: the plain layout, bit \texttt{t} of the bit array with the word number \texttt{w} for the numerator \texttt{rbaLength w + t}, where bit \texttt{t} stands for the numerator \texttt{a₀ + 2\textasciicircum{}k (rbaLength w + t)} of the packing of the 2-adic class of \texttt{b} (stages E and F); indices for the pointers into the survivors, and a scan that holds its position as an index and reads the words of the bit array that it finds in place, where ratpoints recovers the word number from a pointer difference and copies the bit array; the sentinel \texttt{\textasciitilde{}zero} of every build as \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaPack} words \texttt{\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}\textasciitilde{}0}, written one at a time, and the reads \texttt{EXT0} and \texttt{EXT} as words of the array, for the vector type of the build, with one loop over the words of a bit array for the read of the first word and the loop over the others; natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s (stages D and F); no count of the bit arrays that survive the first stage (\texttt{n\_arrays}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli during the run (stage F).)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry.row}: the pattern of one period from \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry.admits}, laid out in words by windows into its packed form, for the builders of \texttt{init.c}, which step through the residues \texttt{a b⁻¹ mod p} four at a time and rotate the pattern through the words, one function for each prime that the build generates, and for the pattern \texttt{sieves0} that the build generates for the row of \texttt{0} (stage F); a fresh array, for the space that the builders take from the buffer of the tables (\texttt{ba\_next}), and the row returned, where the builders also store it in the field \texttt{sieve} of the entry, with a release store for the threads (\texttt{RP\_PUBLISH}), which the thunks of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry.rows} do; the copies of the first bit arrays that the builders append at the end of a row, which only the chunked first stage reads, are none in the build of the model (\texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHUNK} = 1; stage F).)

\end{itemize}
